rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Individual - coping skills could be tested during a crisis, opportunities to learn new coping skills, usual ways of coping may not be available (e.g., not safe to take a walk or not able to talk with friends).
rows.ne: • व्यक्ति — सङ्कटका बेला परिस्थितिको सामना गर्ने सीपको परीक्षा हुन सक्छ, परिस्थितिको सामना गर्ने नयाँ सीप सिक्ने अवसरहरू मिल्न सक्छन् र परिस्थितिको सामना गर्ने सामान्य तरिकाहरू उपलब्ध नहुन सक्छन् (जस्तै, हिँडडुल गर्न जानु सुरक्षित नहुनु वा साथीहरूसँग कुराकानी गर्न नसक्नु)।
rows.bt: • Individual — During a crisis, skills for coping with the situation may be tested, opportunities to learn new skills for coping with the situation may arise, and usual ways of coping with the situation may not be available (for example, it may not be safe to go for a walk or it may not be possible to talk with friends).
rows.note: Coping skills is translated as ordinary, nonclinical wording. A proposal is listed because the term recurs within this row.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Relationships - separation from or loss of loved ones, an increased sense of closeness within a family, increase in relationship violence including GBV.
rows.ne: • सम्बन्ध — प्रियजनहरूबाट अलग हुनु वा उनीहरूलाई गुमाउनु, परिवारभित्र निकटताको अनुभूति बढ्नु, लैङ्गिकतामा आधारित हिंसा (GBV) लगायत सम्बन्धभित्र हुने हिंसा बढ्नु।
rows.bt: • Relationships — Being separated from loved ones or losing them, an increased feeling of closeness within the family, increased violence within relationships, including gender-based violence (GBV).
rows.note: General discussion of relationship violence, not a verbatim safeguarding declaration. Safety review remains pending.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Communities - people who are marginalized may face further discrimination and be unable to access services, community members may feel a stronger sense of cohesion in the face of adversity and help one another.
rows.ne: • समुदाय — सीमान्तीकृत व्यक्तिहरूले थप भेदभाव सामना गर्नुपर्ने र सेवामा पहुँच पाउन नसक्ने हुन सक्छ; प्रतिकूल परिस्थितिमा समुदायका सदस्यहरूले आपसी एकताको अझ बलियो अनुभूति गर्न र एकअर्कालाई सहयोग गर्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: • Community — Marginalized people may have to face additional discrimination and may be unable to access services; in adverse circumstances, community members may feel a stronger sense of mutual unity and help one another.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Services - services may be disrupted (e.g., buildings damaged, staff displaced), new services may be made available by humanitarian responders.
rows.ne: • सेवा — सेवाहरू अवरुद्ध हुन सक्छन् (जस्तै, भवनहरू क्षतिग्रस्त हुनु, कर्मचारीहरू विस्थापित हुनु), मानवीय प्रतिकार्यमा संलग्न पक्षहरूले नयाँ सेवाहरू उपलब्ध गराउन सक्छन्।
rows.bt: • Services — Services may be disrupted (for example, buildings being damaged, staff being displaced), and parties involved in the humanitarian response may provide new services.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Society - economic conditions may worsen, resources may be allocated to services that were previously underfunded.
rows.ne: • समाज — आर्थिक अवस्था बिग्रन सक्छ, पहिले अपर्याप्त रकम उपलब्ध गराइएका सेवाहरूका लागि स्रोतहरू विनियोजन हुन सक्छन्।
rows.bt: • Society — The economic situation may worsen, and resources may be allocated to services that were previously provided with insufficient funds.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: Humanitarian emergencies cause widespread suffering, affecting people’s mental health and psychosocial well-being.
rows.ne: मानवीय आपत्कालीन अवस्थाले व्यापक पीडा निम्त्याउँछ र मानिसहरूको मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याणमा प्रभाव पार्छ।
rows.bt: Humanitarian emergencies cause widespread suffering and affect people's mental health and psychosocial well-being.
rows.note: Psychosocial well-being retains the cited unreviewed T005 candidate; no new clinical terminology is introduced.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • For children, adverse conditions in emergencies can disrupt cognitive, emotional, social and physical development, with enduring consequences for their future.
rows.ne: • बालबालिकाका लागि आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा प्रतिकूल परिस्थितिले संज्ञानात्मक, भावनात्मक, सामाजिक र शारीरिक विकासमा बाधा पुर्‍याउन सक्छन्, जसको उनीहरूको भविष्यमा दीर्घकालीन असर पर्न सक्छ।
rows.bt: • For children, adverse circumstances in emergencies can hinder cognitive, emotional, social and physical development, which can have a long-term effect on their future.
rows.note: The draft retains possibility, all four developmental domains and lasting consequences for children's futures.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Many people affected by emergencies experience common reactions such as difficulties with sleeping, fatigue, worry, anger and physical aches and pains. These are normal reactions to adverse circumstances.
rows.ne: • आपत्कालीन अवस्थाबाट प्रभावित धेरै मानिसहरूले निद्रामा कठिनाइ, थकान, चिन्ता, रिस तथा शारीरिक दुखाइ र पीडाजस्ता सामान्य प्रतिक्रियाहरू अनुभव गर्छन्। यी प्रतिकूल परिस्थितिप्रतिका स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रियाहरू हुन्।
rows.bt: • Many people affected by an emergency experience common reactions such as difficulty sleeping, fatigue, worry, anger, and physical aches and pains. These are natural reactions to adverse circumstances.
rows.note: The examples remain illustrative, and the draft preserves the statement that these are normal reactions without adding a diagnosis.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • For most people, these problems are manageable and will improve over time, but for some people, these problems may persist and affect their ability to do their usual daily tasks.
rows.ne: • अधिकांश व्यक्तिका लागि यी समस्याहरू सम्हाल्न सकिने हुन्छन् र समयसँगै सुधार हुँदै जानेछन्, तर केही व्यक्तिमा यी समस्याहरू रहिरहन सक्छन् र उनीहरूले दैनिक रूपमा गर्ने सामान्य कामहरू गर्ने क्षमतामा असर पार्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: • For most people, these problems are manageable and will improve over time, but in some people these problems may persist and may affect their ability to do the usual tasks they do daily.
rows.note: Drafted as ordinary wording about problems, time and daily functioning; no new clinical label is introduced. Preserves the contrast between most people and some people, and between expected improvement and possible persistence.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Globally one in five people (about 22%) living in an area affected by conflict is estimated to have a mental health condition.4 That is three times the global estimate for people not affected by conflict.5
rows.ne: • विश्वव्यापी रूपमा द्वन्द्वबाट प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा बस्ने प्रत्येक पाँच जनामध्ये एक जना (करिब 22%) मा मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्था हुने अनुमान गरिएको छ।4 यो द्वन्द्वबाट प्रभावित नभएका मानिसहरूका लागि गरिएको विश्वव्यापी अनुमानको तीन गुणा हो।5
rows.bt: • Globally, it is estimated that one in every five people (about 22%) living in conflict-affected areas has a mental health condition.4 This is three times the global estimate for people not affected by conflict.5
rows.note: The draft retains the estimated prevalence, the conflict-affected population, 22%, the threefold comparison and citation markers 4 and 5.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: People with pre-existing mental health conditions are at risk of relapse or deterioration (e.g., disruption of access to psychotropic medication, difficulties coping with additional stressors due to the humanitarian situation) they may be left behind (e.g., if people are fleeing an area) and they need continued access to care and protection.
rows.ne: पहिलेदेखि मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्थाहरू भएका मानिसहरू अवस्था पुनः बल्झिने वा बिग्रिने जोखिममा रहेका हुन्छन् (जस्तै, मनोप्रभावी औषधिसम्मको पहुँचमा अवरोध हुनु, मानवीय परिस्थितिका कारण थपिएका तनावका कारकहरूको सामना गर्न कठिनाइ हुनु)। उनीहरू पछाडि छोडिन सक्छन् (जस्तै, मानिसहरू कुनै क्षेत्रबाट भागिरहेका भएमा), र उनीहरूलाई हेरचाह र संरक्षणमा निरन्तर पहुँच आवश्यक हुन्छ।
rows.bt: People with pre-existing mental health conditions are at risk of the condition recurring or worsening (for example, disruption of access to psychotropic medicines, difficulty coping with additional stress factors caused by humanitarian circumstances). They may be left behind (for example, if people are fleeing an area), and they need continued access to care and protection.
rows.note: The draft retains relapse or deterioration, both contributing examples, the possibility of being left behind and continued access to both care and protection.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: People in mental hospitals and other institutions are especially at risk (e.g., staff fleeing and being displaced, no access to basic needs such as food and water, disruption in medication supply and psychological support)
rows.ne: मानसिक अस्पतालहरू र अन्य संस्थाहरूमा रहेका मानिसहरू विशेष गरी जोखिममा रहेका हुन्छन् (जस्तै, कर्मचारीहरू भाग्नु र विस्थापित हुनु, खाना र पानीजस्ता आधारभूत आवश्यकताहरूमा पहुँच नहुनु, औषधिको आपूर्ति र मनोवैज्ञानिक सहयोगमा अवरोध हुनु)।
rows.bt: People in mental hospitals and other institutions are particularly at risk (for example, staff fleeing and being displaced, lack of access to basic necessities such as food and water, disruption of medicine supplies and psychological support).
rows.note: The draft retains other institutions, heightened risk and every example, including disruption of medication supply and psychological support.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • In your group, discuss and answer the following question. Make a brief presentation on your flip chart and select someone to present it.
rows.ne: • आफ्नो समूहमा निम्न प्रश्नबारे छलफल गर्नुहोस् र उत्तर दिनुहोस्। आफ्नो फ्लिप चार्टमा संक्षिप्त प्रस्तुति तयार गर्नुहोस् र प्रस्तुत गर्न एक जना छान्नुहोस्।
rows.bt: • Discuss and answer the following question in your group. Prepare a brief presentation on your flip chart and choose one person to present.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: In emergencies, people are affected in different ways and require different kinds of services and supports.
rows.ne: आपत्कालीन अवस्था हुँदा मानिसहरू विभिन्न तरिकाले प्रभावित हुन्छन् र उनीहरूलाई विभिन्न किसिमका सेवा र सहयोग आवश्यक पर्छन्।
rows.bt: When an emergency occurs, people are affected in different ways and need different kinds of services and support.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: The intervention pyramid is used to illustrate the range of complementary supports that are required to protect and promote the mental health and psychosocial wellbeing of individuals.
rows.ne: व्यक्तिहरूको मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याणको संरक्षण तथा प्रवर्द्धन गर्न आवश्यक पर्ने एकअर्काका पूरक विभिन्न किसिमका सहयोग देखाउन हस्तक्षेप पिरामिड प्रयोग गरिन्छ।
rows.bt: The intervention pyramid is used to show the different kinds of mutually complementary support needed to protect and promote individuals' mental health and psychosocial well-being.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: If participants are not familiar with the intervention pyramid, explain the following points:
rows.ne: सहभागीहरू हस्तक्षेप पिरामिडसँग परिचित छैनन् भने निम्न बुँदाहरू व्याख्या गर्नुहोस्:
rows.bt: If participants are not familiar with the intervention pyramid, explain the following points:

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • The intervention pyramid communicates a common set of underlying principles:
rows.ne: • हस्तक्षेप पिरामिडले साझा आधारभूत सिद्धान्तहरूको समूह प्रस्तुत गर्छ:
rows.bt: • The intervention pyramid presents a set of shared basic principles:

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Protecting and promoting mental health and psychosocial wellbeing requires a layered system of complementary activities that address different needs
rows.ne: • मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याणको संरक्षण तथा प्रवर्द्धन गर्न विभिन्न आवश्यकतालाई सम्बोधन गर्ने, एकअर्काका पूरक गतिविधिहरूको तहगत प्रणाली आवश्यक पर्छ।
rows.bt: • To protect and promote mental health and psychosocial well-being, a layered system of mutually complementary activities that address different needs is required.
rows.note: T005 is reused from the supplied cited unreviewed candidate.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • All layers of the pyramid are important and should be made available concurrently.
rows.ne: • पिरामिडका सबै तह महत्त्वपूर्ण छन् र तिनलाई एकै समयमा उपलब्ध गराउनु उचित हुन्छ।
rows.bt: • All levels of the pyramid are important, and it is appropriate to make them available at the same time.
rows.note: The back-translation strengthens 'should be made available' to 'must be made available'. The revision expresses a recommendation while retaining all layers and concurrent availability. The back-translation describes concurrent availability as appropriate rather than explicitly stating that all layers should be made available concurrently, weakening the recommendation.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: » Fewer people require services at the higher layers of the pyramid, and a greater number of people require services at the lower layers.
rows.ne: » पिरामिडका माथिल्ला तहका सेवा कम मानिसलाई आवश्यक पर्छन् भने तल्ला तहका सेवा बढी मानिसलाई आवश्यक पर्छन्।
rows.bt: » Fewer people need services at the upper levels of the pyramid, while more people need services at the lower levels.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: » Most people can cope well once their basic needs are met – with basic services and security delivered in ways that protect their dignity
rows.ne: » अधिकांश मानिसका आधारभूत आवश्यकता उनीहरूको मर्यादा जोगिने गरी आधारभूत सेवा र सुरक्षा उपलब्ध गराएर पूरा गरिएपछि उनीहरूले परिस्थितिको राम्रोसँग सामना गर्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: » Once most people's basic needs have been met by providing basic services and security in a way that preserves their dignity, they can cope well with the situation.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: » Many people will benefit from activities that strengthen community and family support
rows.ne: » समुदाय र परिवारको सहयोग सुदृढ गर्ने गतिविधिबाट धेरै मानिस लाभान्वित हुनेछन्।
rows.bt: » Many people will benefit from activities that strengthen community and family support.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: » A smaller number of people will need focused one-to-one care such as MHPSS through individual case management
rows.ne: » अझ कम सङ्ख्याका व्यक्तिहरूलाई एक जनाले एक जनालाई प्रदान गर्ने केन्द्रित हेरचाह आवश्यक हुनेछ, जस्तै व्यक्तिगत केस व्यवस्थापनमार्फत MHPSS।
rows.bt: » An even smaller number of people will need focused care provided by one person to one person, such as MHPSS through individual case management.
rows.note: One-to-one care is rendered descriptively as ordinary service-delivery wording, not as a newly coined clinical intervention name. The comparative 'smaller number' became 'a small number.' 'One person at a time' describes sequencing rather than explicitly preserving the one-to-one care relationship. 'An even smaller number' adds comparative emphasis beyond the source's 'a smaller number.'

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • And an even smaller number need specialized care from psychologists and psychiatrists.
rows.ne: • अनि अझ थोरै सङ्ख्याका मानिसहरूलाई मनोवैज्ञानिकहरू र मनोचिकित्सकहरूबाट विशेषीकृत हेरचाह आवश्यक हुन्छ।
rows.bt: • And an even smaller number of people need specialized care from psychologists and psychiatrists.
rows.note: The draft preserves the smaller comparative group, the need for specialized care and both professional groups.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Individuals that need specialized services, e.g., from a psychiatrist, are also likely to benefit from activities at the lower layers (e.g. support groups, basic services delivered in ways that promote dignity).
rows.ne: • विशेषीकृत सेवाहरू आवश्यक पर्ने व्यक्तिहरूलाई, उदाहरणका लागि मनोचिकित्सकबाट सेवा आवश्यक पर्ने व्यक्तिहरूलाई, तल्ला तहका क्रियाकलापहरूबाट पनि लाभ पुग्ने सम्भावना हुन्छ (जस्तै, सहयोग समूहहरू र मर्यादा प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने तरिकाले प्रदान गरिने आधारभूत सेवाहरू)।
rows.bt: • Individuals who need specialized services, for example individuals who need services from a psychiatrist, are also likely to benefit from lower-level activities (for example, support groups and basic services provided in ways that promote dignity).
rows.note: The draft retains the psychiatrist as an example, the likelihood rather than certainty of benefit, and both examples of lower-layer activities.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Typically, delivering activities at higher layers of the pyramid requires more formal or specialized qualifications. This often corresponds to more training, supervision and mentoring being required for the staff involved.
rows.ne: • सामान्यतया, पिरामिडका माथिल्ला तहमा गतिविधिहरू सञ्चालन गर्न बढी औपचारिक वा विशेषीकृत योग्यता आवश्यक पर्छ। यसअनुसार संलग्न कर्मचारीलाई प्रायः थप तालिम, सुपरिवेक्षण र मार्गदर्शन आवश्यक पर्छ।
rows.bt: • Generally, more formal or specialized qualifications are required to carry out activities at the higher levels of the pyramid. Accordingly, the staff involved often need additional training, supervision and guidance.
rows.note: The recurring standalone term 'pyramid' is absent from the frozen glossary; proposed form: [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]. Qualifications, training and mentoring are ordinary workforce wording here.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • The provision of MHPSS services and activities involves different actors; no single actor/organization can provide all of these activities.
rows.ne: • MHPSS सेवा तथा गतिविधिहरू प्रदान गर्न विभिन्न सम्बद्ध पक्षहरू संलग्न हुन्छन्; कुनै एक पक्ष वा संस्थाले मात्र यी सबै गतिविधि प्रदान गर्न सक्दैन।
rows.bt: • Various relevant parties are involved in providing MHPSS services and activities; no single party or organization alone can provide all these activities.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • The MHPSS response does not involve only MHPSS providers; rather, a wide range of humanitarian actors across different areas of work play an important part (e.g. by ensuring that humanitarian aid is provided in a way that minimized psychological distress and promotes well-being, dignity and agency).
rows.ne: • MHPSS प्रतिकार्यमा MHPSS सेवा प्रदायकहरू मात्र संलग्न हुँदैनन्; बरु, विभिन्न कार्यक्षेत्रमा रहेका मानवीय कार्यमा संलग्न पक्षहरूले महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्छन् (जस्तै, मानवीय सहायता प्रदान गर्दा मानसिक व्यथा न्यून हुने र कल्याण, मर्यादा तथा आफ्ना निर्णय गर्न र तिनअनुसार कार्य गर्न सक्ने क्षमता प्रवर्द्धन हुने कुरा सुनिश्चित गरेर)।
rows.bt: • MHPSS responses do not involve only MHPSS service providers; rather, actors involved in humanitarian work across different sectors play an important role (for example, by ensuring that, when providing humanitarian assistance, mental distress is minimized and well-being, dignity and the ability to make one's own decisions and act on them are promoted).
rows.note: The source's tense mismatch in 'is provided ... minimized' is interpreted as the intended effect of aid delivery; the draft retains the broader range of actors and all four intended outcomes.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: Emphasize
rows.ne: जोड दिनुहोस्।
rows.bt: Emphasize.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: that effective MHPSS programming provides critical services and supports across the life course, taking into account individuals’ needs, vulnerabilities and strengths at different stages of life, particularly at sensitive developmental stages and during more vulnerable periods of life, such as infants, young children, adolescents and older adults.
rows.ne: प्रभावकारी MHPSS कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा कार्यान्वयनले जीवनका विभिन्न चरणमा व्यक्तिका आवश्यकता, जोखिममा पर्न सक्ने अवस्था र सबल पक्षलाई ध्यानमा राख्दै जीवनभर अत्यावश्यक सेवा र सहयोग प्रदान गर्छ। यसमा विशेष गरी विकासका संवेदनशील चरण र जीवनका बढी जोखिमयुक्त अवधि, जस्तै शिशु अवस्था, साना बालबालिकाको अवस्था, किशोरावस्था र ज्येष्ठ वयस्क अवस्थालाई ध्यानमा राखिन्छ।
rows.bt: Effective MHPSS programme planning and implementation provides essential services and support throughout life, taking into account individuals' needs, situations in which they may be at risk, and strengths at different stages of life. Particular attention is given to sensitive stages of development and higher-risk periods of life, such as infancy, the stage of young children, adolescence and older adulthood.
rows.note: Developmental stages and vulnerability are rendered as ordinary life-course wording, not as clinical classifications.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: The aim overall is building individuals resilience and promoting mental health and psychosocial well-being.
rows.ne: समग्र उद्देश्य व्यक्तिहरूमा प्रतिकूल अवस्थाको सामना गरी पुनः अघि बढ्ने क्षमता विकास गर्नु र मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याण प्रवर्द्धन गर्नु हो।
rows.bt: The overall objective is to develop individuals' capacity to face adverse circumstances and move forward again, and to promote mental health and psychosocial well-being.
rows.note: This is an explanatory aim, not a validated instrument item. Resilience is expressed descriptively rather than coined as a clinical term. [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] reuses the cited unreviewed T005 candidate.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: This can lead to improvements in people’s abilities to meet their basic needs to survive, recover and rebuild their lives after difficult experiences.
rows.ne: यसबाट कठिन अनुभवपछि बाँच्न, पुनः सम्हालिन र आफ्नो जीवन पुनर्निर्माण गर्न आवश्यक आधारभूत आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने मानिसहरूको क्षमतामा सुधार आउन सक्छ।
rows.bt: This can improve people's ability to meet the basic needs necessary to survive, recover and rebuild their lives after difficult experiences.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: Remind participants that the social ecological model showed that our mental health and psychosocial wellbeing are impacted by many factors from different layers and areas of our lives, including our health, our physical safety, our access to education, livelihoods, our ability to exercise our legal rights, where we live, community cohesion etc. These are all things that can be severely disrupted by emergencies.
rows.ne: सामाजिक–पारिस्थितिक नमुनाले हाम्रो मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याणमा हाम्रो जीवनका विभिन्न तह र क्षेत्रका धेरै तत्त्वले प्रभाव पार्छन् भन्ने देखाएको थियो भनेर सहभागीहरूलाई सम्झाउनुहोस्। यी तत्त्वमा हाम्रो स्वास्थ्य, शारीरिक सुरक्षा, शिक्षामा पहुँच, जीविकोपार्जन, कानुनी अधिकार प्रयोग गर्ने क्षमता, हामी बस्ने ठाउँ, समुदायको एकता आदि पर्छन्। आपत्कालीन अवस्थाले यी सबैमा गम्भीर अवरोध पुर्‍याउन सक्छ।
rows.bt: Remind participants that the social–ecological model showed that many factors at different levels and in different areas of our lives influence our mental health and psychosocial well-being. These factors include our health, physical safety, access to education, livelihoods, ability to exercise legal rights, the place where we live, community unity, and so on. An emergency can seriously disrupt all of these.
rows.note: This is a facilitator reminder, not an instrument item. [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] reuses the cited unreviewed T005 candidate; the social ecological model is described as a general explanatory model.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: For this reason, to be most effective, MHPSS activities need to focus on many areas of life and must be integrated into different services and areas of work, like health, education, and protection/social services.
rows.ne: यस कारणले, सबैभन्दा प्रभावकारी हुनका लागि MHPSS गतिविधिहरूले जीवनका धेरै क्षेत्रमा ध्यान केन्द्रित गर्नुपर्छ र तिनलाई स्वास्थ्य, शिक्षा तथा संरक्षण/सामाजिक सेवाजस्ता विभिन्न सेवा र कार्यक्षेत्रमा एकीकृत गर्नुपर्छ।
rows.bt: For this reason, to be most effective, MHPSS activities must focus on many areas of life and must be integrated into different services and fields of work, such as health, education and protection/social services.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: This is why MHPSS is a cross-cutting area of work.
rows.ne: यसैले MHPSS विभिन्न क्षेत्रभरि फैलिएको कार्यक्षेत्र हो।
rows.bt: Therefore, MHPSS is a field of work that extends across various sectors.
rows.note: 'Connected with various sectors' weakens 'cross-cutting' to an association; the source describes a field spanning sectors.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: It cuts across several areas of work, such as health, protection (including child protection, gender-based violence, mine action), nutrition, food security and livelihoods, etc.
rows.ne: यो स्वास्थ्य, संरक्षण (बाल संरक्षण, लैङ्गिक हिंसा र बारुदी सुरुङ सम्बन्धी कार्यसहित), पोषण, खाद्य सुरक्षा तथा जीविकोपार्जन आदिजस्ता विभिन्न कार्यक्षेत्रमा फैलिएको छ।
rows.bt: It extends across various fields of work such as health, protection (including child protection, gender-based violence and landmine-related work), nutrition, food security and livelihoods, and so on.
rows.note: Reclassified as an ordinary description of sectors, not a safeguarding declaration or safety procedure. Supplied sector labels are retained as unreviewed candidates. 'Is connected with' replaces the source's assertion that MHPSS cuts across the listed areas of work. 'Mine action' is narrowed to 'landmine-related work.'

rows.ne: जुनसुकै विशिष्ट पिरामिड भए पनि तिनले एउटै साझा सिद्धान्त देखाउँछन्—बहु-तहका पूरक सेवाहरू आवश्यक हुन्छन्—यद्यपि निश्चित क्रियाकलापहरू कुन तहमा राख्नुपर्छ भन्ने कुरा प्रायः फरक हुन्छ (MSP IASC पिरामिडसम्बन्धी वितरण सामग्री पनि हेर्नुहोस्)।

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • In the past, when an emergency happened that was too big for the government to cope with alone, what often happened is that many international actors would rush in to help, without necessarily talking to each other or coordinating their activities well.
rows.ne: • विगतमा, सरकारले एक्लै सामना गर्न नसक्ने गरी ठूलो आपत्कालीन अवस्था आइपर्दा, प्रायः धेरै अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सम्बद्ध पक्षहरू मद्दत गर्न हतारिँदै आइपुग्थे, तर उनीहरूले एकअर्कासँग कुराकानी गरेका वा आफ्ना गतिविधिहरूको राम्रो समन्वय गरेका हुन्थे नै भन्ने हुँदैनथ्यो।
rows.bt: • In the past, when an emergency so large that the government could not cope alone occurred, many international parties involved would often rush in to help, but they would not necessarily have talked to one another or coordinated their activities well.
rows.note: The source says the influx often occurred without communication or good coordination necessarily taking place. Nepali makes absence of communication or coordination categorical within those occurrences; the revision restores 'not necessarily'.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • This could sometimes make things worse rather than better – with lots of people using up resources, and not necessarily working together in an effective way (duplication, gaps, using up resources, unpredictable responses, exploitation).
rows.ne: • यसले कहिलेकाहीँ अवस्था सुधार्नुको सट्टा झन् बिगार्न सक्थ्यो—धेरै मानिसले स्रोतहरू प्रयोग गरेर सकाउँथे र उनीहरूले प्रभावकारी रूपमा मिलेर काम गर्छन् भन्ने सुनिश्चित हुँदैनथ्यो (कामको दोहोरोपन, कमीहरू, स्रोतहरू प्रयोग गरेर सकाउनु, पूर्वानुमान गर्न नसकिने प्रतिकार्य, शोषण)।
rows.bt: • This could sometimes make the situation worse instead of improving it—many people would use up resources, and it was not assured that they would work together effectively (duplication of work, gaps, using up resources, unpredictable response, exploitation).
rows.note: Exploitation is retained as a listed consequence, not expanded into a safeguarding declaration. Both occurrences of 'using up resources' became ordinary resource consumption, weakening the source's depletion meaning.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Thankfully, over the years, having learned many lessons along the way, the humanitarian system has evolved and introduced formal systems to improve the effectiveness of emergency responses.
rows.ne: • सौभाग्यवश, वर्षौँको अवधिमा धेरै पाठ सिक्दै मानवीय प्रणाली विकसित भएको छ र आपत्कालीन प्रतिकार्यको प्रभावकारिता सुधार्न औपचारिक प्रणालीहरू लागू गरेको छ।
rows.bt: • Fortunately, over the years, the humanitarian system has evolved while learning many lessons and has implemented formal systems to improve the effectiveness of emergency response.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • One of the main improvements was the introduction of the Humanitarian Cluster System in 2005.
rows.ne: • प्रमुख सुधारमध्ये एउटा 2005 मा मानवीय क्लस्टर प्रणाली लागू गरिनु थियो।
rows.bt: • One of the major improvements was the introduction of the humanitarian cluster system in 2005.
rows.note: This is a historical explanatory statement, not an instrument item. The source year is retained exactly. rows.en: • They are designated by the Inter Agency Standing Committee (IASC), with responsibility for coordination across organizations and with other clusters.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • Each cluster has a lead agency (as shown on the slide) that provides support to field operations.

rows.bt: • Each cluster has a leading body (as shown on the slide), which provides support for operations on the ground.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: If needed, explain that the cluster approach seeks to:

rows.en: • improve coordination by grouping humanitarian organizations, both UN and non-UN, according to these sectors of humanitarian action,

rows.bt: • To improve coordination by grouping humanitarian organizations within the UN and outside the UN according to these areas of humanitarian work.

rows.en: • formalize the responsibilities of the agencies in charge of leading each grouping.

rows.bt: • To formalize the responsibilities of the agencies assigned to lead each group.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • support the provision of services through a platform that makes it possible to agree on approaches and eliminate duplication of efforts
rows.ne: • अपनाइने पद्धतिमा सहमति जुटाउन र प्रयासको दोहोरोपन हटाउन सम्भव बनाउने साझा मञ्चमार्फत सेवा प्रदान गर्न सहयोग गर्ने।
rows.bt: • To support service delivery through a shared platform that makes it possible to reach agreement on the approach to be adopted and eliminate duplication of effort.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: • promote strategic decision-making: coordination of needs assessment, gap analysis and priority setting, funding needs
rows.ne: • रणनीतिक निर्णय प्रक्रियालाई प्रवर्धन गर्नुहोस्: आवश्यकताहरूको लेखाजोखा, अन्तर विश्लेषण र प्राथमिकता निर्धारणको समन्वय, वित्तपोषणका आवश्यकताहरू।
rows.bt: • Promote the strategic decision-making process: coordination of needs assessment, gap analysis and prioritization, financing needs.

rows.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in Humanitarian Crises
rows.en: In 2019, the global leadership for the inter-agency humanitarian response system (the IASC Principals) re-affirmed the decision to “treat MHPSS as a cross-cutting issue that has relevance within health, protection, nutrition, education and Camp Coordination and Camp Management sectors/clusters, in all emergencies”.6 Other sectors, such as WASH, Shelter & Settlements, Food Security and Livelihoods, can also contribute to the MHPSS response.
rows.ne: 2019 मा, संस्थाहरूबीचको मानवीय प्रतिकार्य प्रणालीको विश्वस्तरीय नेतृत्व (IASC Principals) ले “सबै आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा स्वास्थ्य, संरक्षण, पोषण, शिक्षा तथा शिविर समन्वय तथा शिविर व्यवस्थापन क्षेत्र/क्लस्टरमा सान्दर्भिक हुने, विभिन्न क्षेत्रलाई समेट्ने विषयका रूपमा MHPSS लाई लिने” निर्णयलाई पुनः पुष्टि गर्‍यो।6 खानेपानी, सरसफाइ तथा स्वच्छता (WASH), आश्रय तथा बस्ती, खाद्य सुरक्षा तथा जीविकोपार्जन जस्ता अन्य क्षेत्रले पनि MHPSS प्रतिकार्यमा योगदान गर्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: In 2019, the global leadership of the interagency humanitarian response system (IASC Principals) reaffirmed the decision to “consider MHPSS as a topic encompassing different sectors, relevant to the health, protection, nutrition, education, and camp coordination and camp management sectors/clusters in all emergencies.”6 Other sectors such as water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), shelter and settlements, food security and livelihoods can also contribute to the MHPSS response.
